name: Rolando fracture (comminuted thumb base)
aliases: T- or Y-shaped intra-articular thumb base fracture

reference.source: Rockwood and Green's Fractures in Adults
clinicalPearls: A comminuted intra-articular fracture of the base of the first metacarpal, classically with a T- or Y-shaped configuration and three or more fragments
Effectively a comminuted counterpart of the two-part Bennett fracture, but with a poorer prognosis
The same deforming muscular forces apply, with abductor pollicis longus and adductor pollicis destabilising the fragments
The mechanism is usually a higher-energy axial load on the thumb metacarpal
Management depends on the pattern of comminution: internal fixation for larger reconstructable fragments, and Kirschner-wire or bridging/external fixation for severe fragmentation
CT is valuable for mapping the articular fragments and planning reconstruction
There is a high risk of post-traumatic trapeziometacarpal arthritis despite treatment
reference.pathophysiology: A higher-energy axial load applied to the thumb metacarpal produces a comminuted intra-articular fracture, typically dividing the base into a T- or Y-shaped configuration with dorsal and volar articular fragments. As with the Bennett pattern, the abductor pollicis longus and adductor pollicis exert displacing forces, but the multifragmentary nature of the injury makes anatomical restoration of the joint surface difficult. Impaction and fragmentation of the articular surface disturb the congruity of the highly mobile trapeziometacarpal joint, predisposing to stiffness and degenerative arthritis.
additionalInvestigations: Anteroposterior, lateral and oblique thumb radiographs
A dedicated true anteroposterior view of the trapeziometacarpal joint (Robert view)
CT to map comminution and articular impaction and to plan fixation
Assessment of articular congruity and fragment size
redFlags: Articular impaction with loss of joint congruity
reference.prognosis: Outcomes are generally poorer than for the Bennett fracture because of comminution; severe articular fragmentation predisposes to stiffness and trapeziometacarpal arthritis even after appropriate treatment.
pitfalls: Attempting rigid internal fixation of unreconstructable comminution
Under-imaging by omitting CT to define the fragment pattern
Underestimating the risk of post-traumatic arthritis
Failing to maintain length and alignment against the deforming muscular pull
references: Rockwood and Green's Fractures in Adults
